None appears for the applicant.
Shri Ajay Tamrakar, Advocate, who is in the panel of Advocates prepared by Legal Aid Committee and has a vast experience of arguing the criminal matters, is present in the Court.
He was requested to argue on behalf of the applicant.
Shri Ajay Tamrakar, Advocate, accepted the request made by the Court.
He after going through the record, argued the matter on behalf of the applicant.

This Criminal Revision under Sections 397, 401 of Cr.P.C. has been filed against the judgment and sentence dated 17-4- 1999 passed by Sessions Judge, Raisen in Criminal Appeal No.35/1996 arising out of judgment and sentence dated 3-4-1996 passed by C.J.M., Raisen in Criminal Case No.279/1988 by which 2 Criminal Revision No.792/1999 [Ramnarain Vs. State of M.P.] the applicant has been convicted under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a) (i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and has been sentenced to undergo the rigorous imprisonment of 6 months and a fine of Rs.1000/- with default imprisonment.

sentences.text: The necessary facts for the disposal of the present revision in short are that on 27-2-1988 at about 9:30 A.M., the Food Inspector, S.C.Gupta found that the applicant was going in front of Usha Restaurant, Begumganj and was carrying 4 liters of milk for selling purposes.

A notice for purchasing milk was given in Form No. 6, Ex. P.7, and after making payment of Rs.3/-, he Ramnarain vs State Of M.P. on 16 November, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81425364/
1 purchased 750 M.L. of milk from the applicant.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the purchased milk was made homogeneous.
The milk was stored in clean and dry glass bottles and after adding 20 drops of Formalin, labels Ex.P.8 were affixed.
The signatures of the applicant and two independent witnesses were obtained on the label.
The Panchnama of the proceedings Ex. P.9 was prepared.
One bottle along with form No.7 was sent to Public Analyst, Bhopal on 29-2-1988.
The remaining two bottles were deposited in the office of Local Health Authority, Raisen.
The milk was found adulterated.
Permission was obtained for prosecution.
Notice under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Ex. P.17, was sent by registered post, and the postal receipt is Ex. P.18.
The complaint was filed against the applicant on 23-5-1988.
The applicant abjured his guilt and pleaded not guilty.

The prosecution in order to prove its case,
examined S.C. Gupta (P.W.1), Bhagirath Prasad (P.W.2).
The applicant examined P.P. Gupta (D.W.1) in his defence.

The Trial Court after considering the oral evidence as well as the documentary evidence, held the applicant guilty under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a) (i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced him to undergo the rigorous imprisonment of six months and a fine of Rs.1000/-
with default 3 Criminal Revision No.792/1999 [Ramnarain Vs. State of M.P.] imprisonment.

Being aggrieved by the judgment and sentence passed by the Trial Court, the applicant filed a criminal appeal, which too has suffered dismissal by Judgment dated 17-4-1999 passed by Sessions Judge, Raisen in Criminal Appeal No.35/1996.
It is submitted by the Counsel for the applicant that the Courts below have not appreciated the evidence in proper perspective and the mandatory provisions were not complied with.
S.C. Gupta (P.W.1) has stated that he was appointed as Sanitary Inspector and the State Govt. by notification, Ex. P.1, had appointed all the Sanitary Inspectors as Food Inspector.
The appointment order is Ex. P.3 and he has passed the examination of Sanitary Inspector which is Ex. P.2.
This witness had jurisdiction over the entire Raisen Revenue Division.
The Dy. Directors have been given authority to grant sanction by notification Ex. P.5.

This witness has further stated that on 27-2-1988,
the applicant was going on his bicycle and was having 4 liters of milk for selling purposes.
He was going towards Begumganj town.
On query, the applicant informed that he was carrying cow-buffalow mixed milk and is selling the same at the rate of Rs.4/- per liter.
The applicant agreed to sell 750 M.L. of milk for a consideration of Rs.3/-.
The consideration amount was paid and receipt Ex. P.6 was obtained.
The milk was made homogeneous and milk was stored in three dry and clean bottles and 20 drops of formalin were added in each bottle.
Labels were affixed and the signatures of the applicant and the independent witnesses were obtained and the panchnama Ex.P.9 was prepared.
It is further stated that one sample was sent to the Public Analyst along with Form No.7 Ex.P.10.
The seal was also sent.
The acknowledgment of receipt of sample by the office of Public Analyst is Ex.P.12 and the Local Authority letter is Ex.P.13.
The report of the Public Analyst is Ex.P.14, according to which, the milk was found adulterated.

The permission for 4 Criminal Revision No.792/1999 [Ramnarain Vs. State of M.P.] prosecution was sought by letter Ex. P.15 and the permission is Ex. P.16.

sentences.text: The applicant did not file any application under Section 13 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for retesting.
Although the independent witness Bhagirath Prasad (P.W.2) has turned hostile, but the evidence of the Food Inspector can be relied upon, if the same is found worth reliance.
The Counsel for the applicant could not point out any circumstance, which may make the evidence of the Food Inspector, unreliable.

Even otherwise, while exercising revisional power under Sections 397, 401 of Cr.P.C., this Court cannot substitute its findings of fact and the findings of facts recorded by the Courts below cannot be interfered with unless and until they are found to be perverse or contrary to record.
No perversity could be pointed out by the Counsel for the applicant.
Accordingly, it is held that the applicant is guilty under Sections 7(1) and (16)(1)(a) (i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
It is submitted by the Counsel for the applicant that the incident took place in the year 1988 and more than 29 years have passed.
The applicant faced the ordeal of trial for 8 long years.
Therefore, a lenient view may be adopted while imposing jail sentence.

The submission made by the Counsel for the applicant cannot be accepted as the minimum sentence of six months with fine has been provided under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and the Trial Court has already awarded the minimum sentence.
The conviction of the applicant under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is hereby maintained.
5 Criminal Revision No.792/1999 [Ramnarain Vs. State of M.P.]

The applicant is on bail.
His bail bonds and surety bonds are hereby cancelled.
The applicant is directed to immediately surrender before the Trial Court for undergoing the remaining jail sentence.
The revision fails and is hereby dismissed.
